summary: Redwood ran through a SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review focusing on how evidence is delivered, audit log lineage, RBAC/SSO access for the Trust Center, and KMS/encryption options. Customer asked clarifying questions on data residency and log retention; SE committed to a hands-on demo of audit export and key rotation. Next steps agreed: share reports, customer to map control owners, schedule demo and follow-up legal checks.
topics: Trust Center read-only access and RBAC
Audit logs: retention, lineage, and export
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: okay uh hey everyone thanks for joining, we we have about 50 minutes, we want to run through the posture review and the evidence delivery playbook. um Marcus will cover audit logs and KMS flow.
[00:12] Sarah Patel: thanks lena, appreciate it. to kick off — our timeline is end of Q1 for cert, so the big asks are access to reports, RBAC patterns for trust center, and how logs get exported for audits.
[00:28] Marcus Kim: great, i'll keep it practical. quick agenda: (1) trust center access and RBAC, (2) evidence delivery options and playbook, (3) audit log lineage and retention, (4) encryption/KMS model and key rotation.
[00:42] Tom Ellis: small note — we run in eu-west and us-central, residency is a hard requirement for some PII assets.
[00:50] Lena Ortiz: yup noted. so first, trust center access. lena: we provide read-only Trust Center urls and can create role-based accounts. typically AE creates an org-level view and SE can create a read-only security reviewer role.
[01:04] Priya Rao: when you say role-based, is it SAML SSO integrated or do we need separate credentials?
[01:10] Marcus Kim: we support SAML 2.0 SSO, Okta/ADFS. for partners without SSO we can provision scoped accounts and enforce MFA. sometimes the auto-import of group membership can be imperfect, so we advise a one-time sync and manual mapping.
[01:26] Sarah Patel: ok good. and audit logs — how long are they kept? we need 12 months for certain controls, and some financial artifacts need 7 years.
[01:36] Marcus Kim: default retention for high-fidelity audit logs is 3 months in hot storage, then archived to cold object storage for up to 7 years, configurable per customer. export is via signed S3 export with envelope encryption.
[01:50] Diego Fuentes: envelope encryption meaning our KMS or Redwood-managed key?
[01:54] Marcus Kim: both options. envelope uses a data key encrypted by a master key. customers can use their own AWS KMS or bring-your-own-HSM via our Private deployment integrations — there is an extra ops step for rotation and audit.
[02:08] Sarah Patel: rotation cadence? we prefer 90-day rotation for data keys and annual for master keys.
[02:13] Marcus Kim: yes we can configure data-key rotation at 90 days; master key rotation needs coordination — we have runbooks for key rollover to avoid re-encrypt storms, it's in the trust center docs.
[02:24] Tom Ellis: about evidence delivery playbook — what are the ways we can get evidence? direct portal download, s3 pickup, or pull via API?
[02:33] Lena Ortiz: exactly those three. we typically do: (A) Trust Center direct download (read-only roles), (B) automated scheduled S3 export with signed URLs + envelope encryption, (C) API-backed pull for integrations into ticketing systems. we recommend S3 export for high-volume artifacts.
[02:50] Priya Rao: any PII redaction? can we get redacted copies for external auditors?
[02:55] Marcus Kim: we have redaction filters for certain logs and we can provide redacted report variants in the trust center. full raw logs are available via S3 with appropriate roles. there have been cases where names get transcribed incorrectly in logs, so we do a quick review step when requested — but that's manual.
[03:12] Sarah Patel: okay good. one thing: log-lineage — auditors always ask for chain-of-custody. how do you show that?
[03:20] Marcus Kim: we add immutable markers in the log metadata (UUIDs, origin service, sequence) and every export is signed; the trust center shows export history and checksums. for extra assurance we can add an external signature step — e.g., sign manifests with your KMS key.
[03:36] Diego Fuentes: is the manifest human readable? we'd like to ingest it into our CMDB.
[03:40] Marcus Kim: yes CSV or JSON manifest options, with columns for artifact id, sha256, timestamp, service, control mapping tag.
[03:47] Sarah Patel: control mapping tag — can you map logs to SOC 2 controls?
[03:51] Lena Ortiz: we include control tags per artifact. we also provide a controls matrix export — it's a mapping between Redwood controls and SOC 2/ISO 27001 clauses. we'll share the spreadsheet.
[04:02] Tom Ellis: on RBAC, we need separation of duties, i.e., auditors shouldn't be able to initiate exports. is that supported?
[04:08] Marcus Kim: yes role-based permissions are granular. read-only roles can view and download, but export scheduling and key management require a higher privilege role. these roles can be mapped to SAML groups.
[04:20] Priya Rao: legal question — if we request raw logs for an audit and they contain EU PII, what's the transfer mechanism?
[04:27] Marcus Kim: for EU-resident PII we recommend running export to an EU S3 bucket under your account; if we host the bucket we can restrict region and apply data residency controls. transfers are over TLS and artifacts are encrypted at rest with your KMS.
[04:43] Sarah Patel: can you walk us through a sample evidence delivery timeline? say auditor requests logs today, how long until we can hand over?
[04:52] Lena Ortiz: typical timeline: if artifacts exist in hot store it's minutes to hours (generate manifest, sign, share link). if in cold archive, rehydration may be hours. we can provide SLA options for expedited retrieval.
[05:04] Tom Ellis: any gotchas around re-encryption during key rotation? we've had outages before.
[05:10] Marcus Kim: we avoid full re-encrypts by doing envelope rewraps and background rekeying with a rolling window. the runbook includes a preflight check and staged cutover. Diego, we'll demo that.
[05:22] Sarah Patel: on reports — do you share full SOC 2 Type II report or a redacted version?
[05:27] Lena Ortiz: we share a redacted copy for initial review and provide the full report under an NDA if needed. the Trust Center has a section for compliance artifacts and you can request evidence packages scoped to specific controls.
[05:40] Priya Rao: NDA process — timeline?
[05:43] Lena Ortiz: 24-48 hours typically once legal accepts the template. we'll send our NDA and the redacted report link.
[05:50] Marcus Kim: quick note: for Private deployment customers we can provide SOC attestations for the deployed package as part of the contract; there's an extra step for on-prem evidence collection.
[05:59] Diego Fuentes: for the demo, can you show the manifest CSV and a KMS key rotation example?
[06:04] Marcus Kim: yes we'll set up a short SE session. Diego, what's your timezone preferred window?
[06:08] Diego Fuentes: mornings CET are best.
[06:10] Lena Ortiz: ok we'll propose slots next week.
[06:14] Sarah Patel: one more — retention policy and legal hold. auditors may ask to preserve artifacts beyond retention, can you support a hold flag?
[06:23] Marcus Kim: yes there's an archival hold feature in Trust Center; we can tag artifacts as legal-hold which prevents deletion and preserves manifests.
[06:31] Tom Ellis: nice. small nit — we've seen misspelled service names in metadata before, it's minor but makes mapping messy. can we standardize tags?
[06:39] Marcus Kim: good point. we enforce canonical service ids in the manifest (service_id) and recommend customers map to their internal catalog via our exported fields.
[06:49] Priya Rao: last legal item — KMS audit trail. does Redwood surface key usage logs?
[06:55] Marcus Kim: yes access to key usage events is available. if using your KMS, you can pull CloudTrail logs; if using Redwood-managed KMS, we provide a key-usage report in the Trust Center.
[07:06] Lena Ortiz: ok wrap-up. action items and owners captured. we'll share the redacted SOC 2 and controls matrix, schedule demo for log-lineage and key rotation. any objections?
[07:16] Sarah Patel: no objections. thanks everyone.
[07:20] Tom Ellis: thanks.
[07:22] Priya Rao: thanks all.
[07:25] Lena Ortiz: bye folks.
[07:30] [meeting end — 52 minutes total — further discussion moved to email about NDA details and demo scheduling]
